## General CAP/DA eligibility criteria

Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2**, a person generally must:

- **Be enrolled in NC Medicaid**  
  - Policy says: “**An eligible beneficiary shall be enrolled in the NC Medicaid Program**.”  
  - **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:2.1.1**.  
  - Document effective date: **2025-09-01**.  
  - Amendment status: **No amendment returned; authoritative document is the current 3K-2 policy**.

- **Be in Medicaid Direct (fee-for-service)**  
  - The CAP/DA-specific Medicaid section says the person **“is enrolled in fee-for-services (Medicaid Direct)”**.  
  - **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17**.

- **Need a nursing-facility level of care / institutional level of care**  
  - The policy requires that the beneficiary:
    - **“is determined to require a level of institutional care under the NC State Medicaid Plan”**, and
    - **“Meets the required HCBS nursing facility LOC as determined by NC Medicaid”**.  
  - **Citations:** Policy **3K-2**, Sections **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17** and **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**.

- **Be part of the waiver target group**  
  - The person must be **“a member of a target group documented in the approved waiver application.”**  
  - **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17**.

- **Meet applicable Medicaid eligibility requirements**  
  - The policy says the person **“meets applicable Medicaid eligibility criteria in Section 2.1.2b.”**  
  - **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17**.  
  - I did not retrieve Section 2.1.2(b) itself here, so I’m limiting this answer to what the text above expressly says.

- **Choose CAP/DA / exercise freedom of choice**  
  - The beneficiary must **“exercise[] freedom of choice by choosing to enter the waiver or maintain enrollment in the waiver”** when the level-of-care and need standards are met.  
  - **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17**.

- **Be assigned a CAP/DA waiver slot**  
  - The policy expressly requires that the person **“is assigned a CAP/DA waiver slot.”**  
  - **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17**.

- **Be able to live safely in a private residence or approved location with supports**  
  - The person must be able to have their **“health, safety and well-being maintained at their primary residence or an approved location with the use of both formal and informal supports.”**  
  - A related coverage section says the beneficiary must be **“Able to maintain health, safety and well-being at their primary private residence or an approved location with the use of both formal and informal supports.”**  
  - **Citations:** Policy **3K-2**, Sections **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17** and **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**.

- **Be age 18 or older**  
  - The CAP/DA Medicaid subsection says the beneficiary **“is age 18 years old and older.”**  
  - **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17**.

## Additional coverage-related requirements in the current policy

The policy’s coverage section also says Medicaid covers CAP/DA when the beneficiary:

- has a **completed CAP assessment** showing a **reasonable indication** they will need at least one CAP/DA HCBS within **30 calendar days** of evaluation;
- has a **signed service plan** authorizing one or more waiver services monthly, or certain short-term equipment/modification/technology;
- has paid care needs that can be maintained **within the average institutional cost** of the CAP/DA waiver;
- has a **primary physician** who can link and coordinate medical services; and
- has an **emergency back-up and disaster plan**.  
- **Citation:** Policy **3K-2**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1**.

## Plain-language summary

In plain English, CAP/DA is generally for an **adult Medicaid Direct beneficiary** who:

- qualifies for **NC Medicaid**,
- needs a **nursing-facility level of care**,
- would otherwise need institutional-level long-term care,
- can be safely served **at home or another approved community setting** with supports,
- has an approved **service plan**,
- has a **waiver slot**, and
- meets the other Medicaid and waiver-specific requirements in Policy 3K-2.

## Sources

- **Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:_s17** (“a. Medicaid”)  
- **Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3K-2:3.2.1** (“3.2.1 Specific criteria covered by Medicaid”)  
- **Authoritative document:** **doc:clinical_policy:3K-2**, effective **2025-09-01**

## Short answer

Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 5B**, NC Medicaid specifically does **not** cover these categories of items/services:

1. **Devices for the beneficiary’s comfort or convenience**, or for the convenience of the beneficiary’s caregiver(s).  
   - **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:4.2.1**.

2. **Backup devices** or **duplicate devices** to keep at different locations.  
   - **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:4.2.1**.

3. **Devices and supplies for residents of nursing facilities.**  
   - **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:4.2.1**.

4. **Devices or supplies covered by another agency.**  
   - **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:4.2.1**.

5. **Equipment or supplies for beneficiaries receiving hospice care**, as defined in Subsection 7.3.  
   - **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:4.2.1**.

In addition, Medicaid does **not** cover a product or service if:
- the beneficiary does not meet **eligibility requirements** in Section 2.0;
- the beneficiary does not meet the **coverage criteria** in Section 3.0;
- it **duplicates another provider’s** procedure, product, or service; or
- it is **experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial**.  
- **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:4.1**.

## General criteria that must be met for coverage

For coverage under Policy 5B, the policy says the procedure, product, or service must be:

### General coverage criteria
- **individualized, specific, and consistent with symptoms or confirmed diagnosis** of the illness or injury being treated, and **not in excess of the beneficiary’s needs**;
- able to be **safely furnished**, with **no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment available statewide**; and
- furnished in a way **not primarily intended for the convenience** of the beneficiary, caregiver, or provider.  
- **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:3.1**.

### Additional orthotics/prosthetics-specific criteria
They must be:
- **ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner**;
- **medically necessary** to maintain or improve the beneficiary’s **medical, physical, or functional level**;
- **appropriate for use in any noninstitutional setting** in which normal life activities take place;
- supported by a **documented face-to-face encounter** with the ordering physician/PA/NP related to the primary reason for the orthotic/prosthetic, occurring **no more than six months prior** to initiation;
- subject to review of the beneficiary’s need by the ordering physician/PA/NP **at least annually**.  
- **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:3.2.1**.

### Device-specific medical necessity standards
The policy also states:

- **Orthotic devices** are medically necessary when required to:
  - **correct or prevent skeletal deformities**,
  - **support or align movable body parts**, or
  - **preserve or improve physical function**.  
  - **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:3.2.1**.

- **Prosthetic devices** are medically necessary as a replacement for all or part of the function of a **permanently inoperative, absent, or malfunctioning body part**, and the beneficiary must require the prosthesis for:
  - **mobility**,
  - **daily care**, or
  - **rehabilitation purposes**.  
  - **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:3.2.1**.

### Other required conditions
Orthotic and prosthetic devices must also be:
- a **reasonable and medically necessary part** of the treatment plan;
- **consistent with the beneficiary’s diagnosis and medical condition**, especially the functional limitations and symptoms; and
- **of high quality**, with **replacement parts available and obtainable**.  
- **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:3.2.1**.

The policy further says that, to be reimbursed, **the provider must be enrolled as an appropriate board-certified provider for the specific device**.  
- **Citation:** Policy **5B**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:5B:3.2.1**.

## Practical takeaway

If you are trying to determine whether a DME-like item is covered under the **Orthotics & Prosthetics** policy, NC Medicaid will deny it under Policy 5B if it is mainly for **comfort/convenience**, is a **backup/duplicate**, is for a **nursing facility resident**, is **covered by another agency**, or falls under **hospice equipment/supplies**. Even if it is not in one of those excluded categories, it still must satisfy the policy’s **medical necessity, ordering, face-to-face, annual review, and provider-enrollment requirements**.

# Outpatient Behavioral Health Services: entrance, continued service, and discharge criteria

## 1) Entrance criteria
Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 8C, Section 3.2.1.1** (**Section ID: `sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.1`**), the beneficiary must meet the following:

- **A current DSM-5 diagnosis**
- The beneficiary presents **behavioral, psychological, or biological dysfunction and functional impairment** consistent with and associated with the current diagnosis
- **If a higher level of care is indicated but unavailable or the beneficiary is refusing the service**, outpatient services can be provided until the appropriate level of care is available or to support the beneficiary to participate in that higher level of care
- The beneficiary is **capable of developing skills to manage symptoms, make behavioral changes, and respond favorably to therapeutic interventions**
- There is **no evidence that alternative interventions would be more effective**, based on North Carolina community practice standards

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy **8C**, Section **3.2.1.1** (`sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.1`), current authoritative document effective **2025-04-15**.

## 2) Continued service criteria
Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 8C, Section 3.2.1.2** (**Section ID: `sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.2`**), continued services require:

### First, **any ONE** of the following:
- The desired outcome or level of functioning has **not been restored, improved, or sustained** over the timeframe outlined in the treatment plan
- The beneficiary **continues to be at risk for relapse** based on current clinical assessment and history
- The **functional gains are tenuous**

### And, **in addition to the above, any ONE** of the following:
- The beneficiary has **achieved current treatment plan goals, and additional goals are indicated** as evidenced by documented symptoms
- The beneficiary is **making satisfactory progress toward meeting goals** and there is documentation that supports that

**Plain-language summary:** For continued outpatient behavioral health, the policy requires both:
1. ongoing clinical need or instability, **and**
2. evidence that treatment goals still remain or that the person is progressing in treatment.

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy **8C**, Section **3.2.1.2** (`sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.2`), current authoritative document effective **2025-04-15**.

## 3) Discharge criteria
Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 8C, Section 3.2.1.3** (**Section ID: `sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.3`**), discharge is appropriate when:

- The beneficiary’s **level of functioning has improved** with respect to the goals outlined in the treatment plan
- The beneficiary or legally responsible person **no longer wishes to receive these services**
- The beneficiary, based on presentation and **failure to show improvement despite modifications in the treatment plan**, requires a **more appropriate best practice or evidence-based treatment modality** based on North Carolina community practice standards

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy **8C**, Section **3.2.1.3** (`sec:doc:clinical_policy:8C:3.2.1.3`), current authoritative document effective **2025-04-15**.

# Bottom line
For **NC Medicaid outpatient behavioral health services**, Policy **8C** says:

- **Entrance**: there must be a DSM-5 diagnosis, associated dysfunction/impairment, ability to benefit from therapy, and no better alternative intervention.
- **Continued service**: there must still be ongoing need/risk/tenuous gains **plus** evidence of remaining goals or satisfactory progress.
- **Discharge**: occurs when goals-related functioning improves, the person no longer wants services, or outpatient treatment is no longer the right modality and a more appropriate evidence-based treatment is needed.

per_question.question: Does NC Medicaid cover Personal Care Services for beneficiaries who live in an assisted living facility?
per_question.agent_answer:
I looked at the NC Medicaid **clinical policy for Personal Care Services in congregate settings**, which is the policy that applies to **assisted living/adult care home settings**.

# Short answer

**Yes — NC Medicaid can cover Personal Care Services (PCS) for beneficiaries living in an assisted living facility, but only if they meet the policy’s specific eligibility criteria.**

The governing policy says PCS in congregate settings is available for a beneficiary who:

- has a qualifying medical, mental, disability, or cognitive condition with unmet ADL needs; and
- **resides in “a congregate facility licensed by the State of North Carolina as an Adult Care Home (ACH)”** or certain qualifying group homes.

Because an **assisted living facility** in North Carolina is generally an **Adult Care Home/congregate setting**, this policy is the relevant coverage policy.  
**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy **3L-1**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:3.2.1**.  
Amendment status: **current authoritative document is 3L-1; no amendments were returned by the amendment tool.**

# What the policy specifically requires

Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:3.2.1**, the beneficiary must:

- have a medical or mental condition, disability, or cognitive impairment; and
- demonstrate unmet needs for at least:
  - **three of the five qualifying ADLs with limited hands-on assistance**, or
  - **two ADLs, one requiring extensive assistance**, or
  - **two ADLs, one requiring full dependence-level assistance**.

The same section also says the beneficiary must **reside in**:

- **“a congregate facility licensed by the State of North Carolina as an Adult Care Home (ACH)”**, or
- certain licensed group homes.

And additional criteria in that same section include:

- the congregate setting must be safe and free of hazards;
- no other third-party payer is responsible for PCS;
- no family/household member or informal caregiver is available, willing, and able to provide the authorized services at those times;
- the PCS must be directly linked to a documented condition causing the functional limitations;
- the beneficiary must be under the ongoing direct care of a physician; and
- the beneficiary must be medically stable and **not require continuous care, monitoring, or supervision by a licensed nurse or other licensed health care professional**.

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy **3L-1**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:3.2.1**.

# Important limitation

NC Medicaid does **not** cover PCS in this setting if the person’s needs exceed what a licensed congregate facility can properly meet.  
Policy 3L-1 states PCS in a **licensed congregate facility** is not appropriate where the beneficiary, for example:

- is ventilator dependent;
- requires continuous licensed nursing care;
- has a physician certification that placement is no longer appropriate; or
- has health/medical/functional needs that cannot properly be met in the licensed care home.

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy **3L-1**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:4.2.1.1**.  
Amendment status: **no amendments returned; 3L-1 is the authoritative current document.**

# One more eligibility point

The policy also says that even an otherwise eligible beneficiary may be ineligible if their **Medicaid eligibility category has service restrictions**.  
**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy **3L-1**, Section **sec:doc:clinical_policy:3L-1:2.1.1**.

# Bottom line

NC Medicaid covers **CAR-T cell therapy** when the therapy:

per_question.question: Until what age should physicians provide fluoride varnish applications for Medicaid beneficiaries, and what oral screening requirements apply?

Physicians should provide **fluoride varnish beginning at tooth eruption until the beneficiary is 3½ years of age**.

- **Early caries screening**
- Detection of **notable findings** in the oral cavity using **a dental mirror and directed light**
- **Counseling and educational materials** on oral hygiene and nutrition for children
- **Prescribing a fluoride supplement, if indicated**
- **Documentation** of the oral evaluation, notable findings, caregiver counseling, fluoride varnish application, and **referral to a dentist if appropriate**

**Clinical Coverage Policy 1A-23, Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:1A-23:7.2** states:

  - “**application of fluoride varnish**; and”

Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 12B (HIV Case Management)**, a provider must meet the following **certification requirements**:

- Ensure HIV Case Management services are provided by **qualified case managers** described in **Subsections 6.1.1, 6.1.2, and 6.1.3**.
- Ensure supervision by **qualified supervisors** described in **Subsections 6.1.4 and 6.1.5**.
- **Enroll each physical site** with NC Medicaid as a provider of HIV Case Management services.
- Meet **applicable state and federal laws** governing Medicaid provider participation.
- **Maintain certification** as a qualified provider of HIV Case Management services.
- Demonstrate compliance with **initial and ongoing certification processes**.
- Demonstrate compliance with **monitoring and evaluation of case management records through a quality improvement plan**.
- Allow **NC Medicaid or its designated contractor** to review beneficiary records and inspect agency operations and financial records.
- Notify NC Medicaid or its designated contractor of proposed changes (such as owner/name/address/telephone changes or dissolution plans) **within 30 calendar days of the proposed change**, and **no later than five business days of the actual change**.
- **Within one year of enrollment** with Medicaid as a provider, achieve **national accreditation** from at least one designated accrediting agency: **ACHC, CARF, CHAP, COA, PHAB, The Joint Commission, or URAC**.

- Submit copies of items in **Subsection 6.2.3** that changed since initial certification;
- Submit copies of all **HIV case manager and supervisor credentials**;
- Submit **annual summaries of quality improvement activities**, including outcome metrics; and
- Submit to an **on-site recertification visit**, including review of beneficiary records or other clinical/business documentation as needed.

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy **12B**, **Section sec:doc:clinical_policy:12B:6.2.4**.

A provider can be **decertified** under Policy 12B for any of the following reasons:

- **Failure to develop, submit, and implement a written plan of correction** to resolve unmet program requirements cited by NC Medicaid or its designated contractor, or failure to make recommended corrections, **within 30 calendar days**

- **Violation of a beneficiary’s confidentiality**

- **Failure to implement and enforce a quality improvement program**
- **Failure to notify** NC Medicaid or its designated contractor of changes in agency name, director or ownership, mailing address, or phone number within the required time frames, resulting in inability to contact the provider
- **Failure to comply with all applicable federal and state laws, regulations, state reimbursement plan, and Medicaid policies**
- **Failure to enroll any beneficiaries within four months of certification**
- **Failure to achieve or maintain certification requirements** defined in **Subsection 6.2**
